SHA256: 7c0927f0a84f5938a20ba39908d575f42708f8a13bba0d8042872d2183aa2b33
// Present pacer (pure function, shared by Mac / iOS; unit test tests/t_pace.c).
// Semantics as vsync: present slot = previous present slot + period. Early → wait until the present slot; late by less than one period → present immediately and keep the original phase;
// behind by one period or more (stutter) → restart the cadence from the current time, no burst of presents to catch up. Period 0 = no wait (the present slot follows the current time).
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

typedef struct { uint64_t target; } nvn_pacer;

// now: monotonic clock (ns); period: this frame's period (ns, 0 = no wait). Returns the ns to wait (0 = present immediately) and updates the internal target time.
static inline uint64_t nvn_pace(nvn_pacer *p, uint64_t now, uint64_t period) {
    if (!period || !p->target) { p->target = now; return 0; }
    uint64_t next = p->target + period;
    if (now <= next) { p->target = next; return next - now; }
    p->target = now - next < period ? next : now;
    return 0;
}

// A frame that something other than this beat paced (the display link's ticks, or no pacing at all: present interval 0): the beat follows it and restarts at its present.
// The beat is only a clock while the caller waits for it. Stepped by the period for frames it did not pace, it ran ahead of real time whenever presents came faster than the
// period, without bound (Ocarina of Time on a 120 Hz variable-refresh link: 27.6 s ahead after 18,000 frames), and the fallback that waits for the beat when the display link
// goes silent or times out then slept the whole lead in one go. Restarted here, the fallback's first wait is at most one period from the last present, and nvn_pace steps
// from there; a caller that waits keeps nvn_pace as it is, including a lead of several periods when its swap chain queues frames ahead (three textures: two periods)
static inline void nvn_pace_follow(nvn_pacer *p, uint64_t now) { p->target = now; }

========================================================================
FILE: /Users/maclifedrive/Downloads/nxnative-clean-check/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_fstep.h
========================================================================
SIZE: 21217 bytes
SHA256: ce714c0abca2621c3ca61156d86b2912daa9165dfb2e84b0c22f3045cfde2ffe
// Frame step in whole vsyncs (pure function, shared by Mac / iOS; unit test tests/t_fstep.c). The rewriter's frame-step stubs (patch_nso.py FRAME_STEP: Tears of the Kingdom 1.4.3,
// Breath of the Wild 1.9.0) step the game by the vsyncs (1/60 s) the host hands them each frame, and the host keeps each frame on screen for k vsyncs (hle_nvn.c present_itv).
// At a steady rate the step is the time on screen: even motion, and only steps the games' own interval logic uses (60 / 30 / 20 fps). Real time the game falls behind (a late
// frame, a hitch) is a debt paid back one extra vsync per frame, so over time game time = real time. k follows the frames' cost: three late frames in a row step up to the cost
// (30 fps when 60 does not hold: no 40 fps steps on 120 Hz screens) when the frames at k also fall short of it on average (FSTEP_LATE over the last FSTEP_RUN frames); 30 frames
// in a row on time whose cost, or the mean cost of the hold's frames, would fit k − 1 try it, and a trial that fails waits twice as long before the next (1 s → 8 s), so a device on the edge does not flap.
// The average: a frame late by FSTEP_LATE is the rate of a hold that does not hold (53 fps is not 60), but three such frames in a row among frames on time are not. Frames whose
// cost scatters around k (Mario Kart World on an M4 Max: 20–30% of them 1–5 ms late, 57.5–61 fps and game time 0.99–1.02 of real time with no holds) met three in a row about once
// a second and spent half the time at 30 or 20, up and down 30 times a session (issue #1823); a short hitch (pipeline compiles) stepped to 30 the same way. The late frames are
// paid back by the step, so only a rate that falls short of k is worth a longer hold. Where the step cannot pay them back (120 fps, where the game steps by its target: a late
// frame is slow motion) three late frames still raise the hold. The step goes to the cheapest of the three late frames' cost: a hitch as the third no longer meant 20 fps.
// A game takes steps up to its stub's largest (smax; Mario Kart World's interval logic stops at 2): k and the paid-back step stay within it, or the frames held longer than the
// game steps play in slow motion and the debt counted as paid is lost.
// A probe is a trial back to kmin that the cost does not justify: while the caller reports the CPU slowed for reasons other than heat (an iPhone's performance controller
// parks a game that waits out a long hold on the efficiency cores at half the clock, where its cost never fits k − 1 again), the hold-off alone starts one. Its first
// FSTEP_GRACE frames may be late without failing it, the time the controller needs to raise the clock for the shorter deadline; after them it is judged like a trial.
// A probe that holds leaves the hold-off as it is, and the run at kmin it starts must last FSTEP_HOLD_MAX (8 s) before the hold-off returns to 1 s: a shorter one counts as
// a failed probe, so a CPU that really cannot hold kmin is not probed every second.
// A step up after a run at kmin of FSTEP_HOLD_MAX keeps the cost that held there, and a cost at the longer hold of at most FSTEP_SAME times it starts a probe too: the scene
// costs what it did, so the step up came from a hitch (Breath of the Wild on an iPhone: pipeline compiles after a cutscene). The fit trial alone does not bring such a game
// back: an iPhone lowers its GPU clock until the work fills most of the frame, so a GPU-bound game's cost sits near FSTEP_FIT at either hold (BotW: GPU 12.8–15.2 ms at hold
// 2, p50, where hold 1 had held for minutes; the same 4,900 draws took 5.8 ms after a trip to the background and 13.5 ms half a minute later).
// A cap that falls and rises again (a movie, hle_movie.c dm_movie_hz; the iOS thermal cap in hle_nvn.c) keeps what was learned at each kmin: the cost that held it
// (cref) and the GPU reference (nvn_fgpu below); and the frames after the cap rises are a probe with its grace, as the clocks are still set for the longer hold. Before, the
// rise set k to kmin with no grace, so three frames late while the clock rose stepped up again, with cref dropped at the cap change and a GPU reference taken at the 30 fps
// cap: neither the fit trial (a GPU-bound cost near FSTEP_FIT) nor a probe brought kmin back (t_fstep: the movie and thermal cap cases). A cref kept from before the cap
// starts a probe only when the cost at the longer hold is within FSTEP_SAME of it, and a failed probe doubles the hold-off as any other does.
#pragma once
#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#define FSTEP_MAX 3           // the largest step: both games' own interval logic uses 1–3 (BotW clamps to [2, 3], TOTK picks 2 or 3), so their integer readers never see 4
#define FSTEP_LATE 0.1        // a frame is late when it or its GPU work took this many vsyncs (1.7 ms) more than k: 53 fps is not 60 (start-to-start jitter on time is well below)
#define FSTEP_SHORT_MAX 2.0  // a frame counts at most this many vsyncs past its hold toward the average (a load's stall is one long frame, not a rate)
#define FSTEP_FIT 0.85        // a frame would fit k − 1 when its cost is at most this share of it
#define FSTEP_RUN 30          // frames in a row that fit k − 1 before a trial, and frames a trial must hold
#define FSTEP_DEBT_MAX 15.0   // debt kept at most (0.25 s): the rest of a long stall (a load) is dropped, not replayed
#define FSTEP_HOLD0 60.0      // vsyncs since the last step up before a trial: 1 s, doubled after each failed trial up to 8 s
#define FSTEP_HOLD_MAX 480.0
#define FSTEP_GRACE 30        // a probe's first frames, whose lateness neither fails it nor counts toward a step up (the controller lowered the clock within 10 frames of a step to 30)
#define FSTEP_SAME 1.1        // the cost at the longer hold against the cost that held kmin: at most this much is the same scene (BotW at hold 2: 1.0–1.07 times its hold-1 GPU time)
// The grace is renewed (nvn_fstep.ramp) while the probe's frames keep getting cheaper: a controller that raises the clock slowly is still raising it. macOS raises the GPU clock
// of a game that misses its deadline at 85–100% GPU occupancy by about 100 MHz a second (Breath of the Wild on an M5 Pro: 338 → 432 MHz over a 33-frame probe, GPU 24.8 → 18.5 ms,
// then the probe failed at 22 ms frames; hold 1 needs about 560 MHz there), where the iPhone's controller settles within the 30 frames. A window of FSTEP_GRACE frames whose
// second half cost at most 1 − FSTEP_RAMP of its first half, and had a late frame (a window on time is judged as a trial), starts another, up to FSTEP_PROBE_MAX frames in all
#define FSTEP_RAMP 0.05       // the fall in cost from one half of a grace window to the next that shows the clock still rising (the per-frame noise of a 25 ms frame is 4%, of 15 frames 1%)
#define FSTEP_PROBE_MAX 180   // grace frames a probe may take in all (3 s at 60 fps): a clock that keeps rising without reaching the hold is not waited for longer

typedef struct {
    int k, step;              // vsyncs each frame stays on screen; the step handed to the game for the next frame (k, or k + 1 while paying back)
    int kmin;                 // the last call's kmin (a lower one takes effect at once)
    double debt;              // real time the game is behind, in vsyncs
    int late_run, fit_run, trial;   // late frames in a row; frames in a row whose cost fits k − 1; frames left of a trial at k − 1 (0 = none)
    int probe, grace;         // 1: the trial in progress is a probe; 2: a probe held and its run at kmin has not ended yet; frames left of the probe's grace
    int ramp;                 // set by the caller (kept): 1 = a probe's grace is renewed while its frames keep getting cheaper (FSTEP_RAMP; the host's DM_FSTEP_PROBE_RAMP)
    double pa, pb; int plate, ptotal;   // the current grace window: the cost of its first and second halves (sums), its late frames; grace frames this probe has taken in all
    double hold, since;       // vsyncs a trial waits for after a step up; vsyncs since the last step up
    int per_vsync;            // set by the caller: the ticks a 1/60 s vsync is (0 = 1). At 120 fps the unit is 1/120 s (hle_nvn.c fps_high), and the waits between trials stay the same real time
    double shown_slack;       // vsyncs a frame on time may show longer than k (set by the caller): one refresh on screens whose rate is not a multiple of 60; the cost keeps FSTEP_LATE
    int screen;               // set by the caller before each call, then cleared: 0 = judge lateness by shown and cost; 1 = the screen showed a recent frame on time, 2 = late. With present
                              // snapshots (nvn_mtl.m) the game runs ahead of the screen and a frame that runs long is absorbed, so only what the screen shows counts
    double run, crun, cref;   // vsyncs at kmin in a row; the cost of its frames on time (running mean; not during a probe's trial, whose frames run while the clock rises);
                              // crun when the last run of FSTEP_HOLD_MAX or more ended in a step up or a cap change (0 = none yet)
    double ccur; int ck, cn;  // the cost of the frames on time at the longer hold ck (running mean) and their count
    int ckmin;                // the kmin run, crun and cref belong to
    double cref_at[FSTEP_MAX + 1];   // cref of each kmin, kept while another kmin is in force
    double over[FSTEP_RUN], over_sum; int over_i, over_k;   // the last FSTEP_RUN frames at the hold over_k: shown − k of each (clamped), their sum; the next slot
    double last_cost[3];      // the last three frames' costs, oldest first
    int smax;                 // set by the caller: the largest step the game takes (its stub's STEP_MAX; 0 = FSTEP_MAX)
    int no_payback;           // set by the caller: 1 = the game does not take the step (120 fps: it steps by its target), so three late frames raise the hold whatever the average
    uint64_t late, paid, ups, downs, failed, probes; double dropped;   // statistics for the log
} nvn_fstep;

// A drain of frames standing in the display link's queue in a frame's time (hle_nvn.c fstep_tick, g_fs_drain; nvn_link_drain.h): the acquire waited extra link ticks while the
// screen showed every queued frame for its hold, so the part that made the frame longer than its hold is neither a late frame nor time the game owes: it comes out of the
// frame's time. (The wait for the screen without the link is not one: there a frame longer than its hold is one the screen showed late.) span: time since the previous frame's
// start; hold: the hold the frame had; first: drain in the acquire that started this frame, part of *pacing (its pacing wait); before: drain in later acquires of the previous
// frame, in span but not in *pacing. Returns span less the cut; *pacing loses the cut's part in it (the frame's CPU time, span − pacing, keeps what it was, less the later
// acquires' wait, which was no work either). All in the same unit (ns).
static inline uint64_t nvn_fstep_drain_cut(uint64_t span, uint64_t hold, uint64_t first, uint64_t before, uint64_t *pacing) {
    if (first > *pacing) first = *pacing;
    uint64_t over = span > hold ? span - hold : 0, cut = first + before < over ? first + before : over;
    *pacing -= cut < first ? cut : first;
    return span - cut;
}

// Whether the cost at the longer hold is the cost that held kmin (a probe without a slowed report)
static inline int nvn_fstep_same(const nvn_fstep *s) { return s->cref > 0 && s->cn >= FSTEP_RUN && s->ccur <= FSTEP_SAME * s->cref; }

// Once per frame. shown: real time since the previous frame's start, in vsyncs; cost: the frame's work, max(CPU, GPU), in vsyncs (a GPU that cannot keep up makes frames late too); kmin: 1 at a 60 fps cap, 2 at 30;
// kmax: the longest hold (FSTEP_MAX; 2 at a 30 fps cap, where the display link runs at 30 Hz and holds only even counts); fixed: a step the game has set itself (BotW's
// VFR override; 0 = none), which the host then holds as it is; slow: the CPU runs below its speed for reasons other than heat, so a cost above k − 1 is no evidence
// against kmin (probes). Returns the step for the next frame; s->k is how long that frame stays on screen
static inline int nvn_fstep_next(nvn_fstep *s, double shown, double cost, int kmin, int kmax, int fixed, int slow) {
    const double hold0 = FSTEP_HOLD0 * (s->per_vsync ? s->per_vsync : 1), hold_max = FSTEP_HOLD_MAX * (s->per_vsync ? s->per_vsync : 1);
    if (kmin < 1) kmin = 1;
    const int smax = s->smax > 0 && s->smax < FSTEP_MAX ? s->smax : FSTEP_MAX;
    if (kmax > smax) kmax = smax;
    if (kmin > smax) kmin = smax;
    if (kmax < kmin) kmax = kmin;
    if (!s->hold) s->hold = hold0;
    if (fixed > 0) {   // the game's own step: speed is right by construction, nothing to pay back
        s->k = s->step = fixed < smax ? fixed : smax;
        s->debt = 0; s->late_run = s->fit_run = s->trial = s->probe = s->grace = 0; s->run = 0;
        s->kmin = FSTEP_MAX + 1;   // when it ends, k starts again from kmin
        return s->step;
    }
    if (!s->k) { s->k = s->step = s->kmin = kmin; return s->step; }   // first frame: nothing measured yet
    int held = s->k;   // the frame that just ended stayed on screen this long
    if (held != s->over_k) { s->over_k = held; s->over_sum = 0; s->over_i = 0; memset(s->over, 0, sizeof s->over); }   // judged against the hold in force, not the frames before a step
    double over = shown - held; if (over < -1) over = -1; if (over > FSTEP_SHORT_MAX) over = FSTEP_SHORT_MAX;
    s->over_sum += over - s->over[s->over_i]; s->over[s->over_i] = over; s->over_i = (s->over_i + 1) % FSTEP_RUN;
    s->last_cost[0] = s->last_cost[1]; s->last_cost[1] = s->last_cost[2]; s->last_cost[2] = cost;
    s->debt += shown - s->step;
    if (s->debt > FSTEP_DEBT_MAX) { s->dropped += s->debt - FSTEP_DEBT_MAX; s->debt = FSTEP_DEBT_MAX; }
    if (s->debt < -1) s->debt = -1;   // ahead (a frame shorter than its step): nothing slows the game down, so at most one vsync is remembered
    s->since += shown;
    int cap_probe = kmin < s->kmin && s->kmin <= FSTEP_MAX && s->k > kmin;
    if (cap_probe) {   // the cap rose: a probe at once, whose grace covers the clocks still set for the longer hold
        s->k = kmin; s->probes++; s->trial = FSTEP_RUN; s->probe = 1; s->grace = FSTEP_GRACE; s->fit_run = s->late_run = 0; s->pa = s->pb = 0; s->plate = s->ptotal = 0;
    } else if (kmin < s->kmin || s->k < kmin) s->k = kmin;   // the game's own step ended, or the cap fell
    if (s->k > kmax) s->k = kmax;
    s->kmin = kmin;
    int scr = s->screen; s->screen = 0;
    int late = scr ? scr == 2 : shown > held + FSTEP_LATE + s->shown_slack || cost > held + FSTEP_LATE, grace = s->grace > 0;
    if (grace && !cap_probe) {   // the completed frame at the old cap does not consume the new hold's grace
        if (s->grace > FSTEP_GRACE / 2) s->pa += cost; else s->pb += cost;
        s->plate += late; s->ptotal++;
        if (!--s->grace && s->ramp && s->plate && s->ptotal + FSTEP_GRACE <= FSTEP_PROBE_MAX && s->pb <= (1 - FSTEP_RAMP) * s->pa) { s->grace = FSTEP_GRACE; s->pa = s->pb = 0; s->plate = 0; }   // still getting cheaper: another window
    }
    if (late) { s->late++; s->late_run = grace ? 0 : s->late_run + 1; s->fit_run = 0; } else s->late_run = 0;
    // The cost of the frames on time (a hitch is not what the scene costs): at kmin, and at the longer hold
    if (kmin != s->ckmin) {   // another cap: its run starts over, and what held it before comes back
        if (s->ckmin >= 1 && s->ckmin <= FSTEP_MAX) {
            // A cap can end a sustained run before any hitch saved its cost. Short runs keep the earlier proven reference.
            if (s->run >= hold_max && s->crun > 0) s->cref = s->crun;
            s->cref_at[s->ckmin] = s->cref;
        }
        s->ckmin = kmin; s->run = s->crun = 0; s->cref = kmin <= FSTEP_MAX ? s->cref_at[kmin] : 0;
    }
    // A frame the screen showed on time while its cost did not fit (absorbed by present snapshots) is not what the hold costs: the probes would take it for the scene that held kmin
    int fits = !scr || cost <= held;
    if (held <= kmin) { s->run += shown; s->cn = 0; if (!late && fits && s->probe != 1) s->crun = s->crun > 0 ? s->crun + (cost - s->crun) / 32 : cost; }
    else {
        s->run = 0;
        if (held != s->ck) { s->ck = held; s->cn = 0; }
        if (!late && fits) { s->ccur = s->cn ? s->ccur + (cost - s->ccur) / 8 : cost; s->cn++; }
    }
    // A rate below k over the last FSTEP_RUN frames (the slots not filled yet since the hold changed count as on time); the screen's verdict (present snapshots) is its own
    int short_of_k = scr || s->no_payback || s->over_sum > FSTEP_LATE * FSTEP_RUN;
    if (s->late_run >= 3 && s->k < kmax && short_of_k) {   // step up to the cost of the cheapest of the three late frames, at least one vsync
        double c3 = s->last_cost[0] < s->last_cost[1] ? s->last_cost[0] : s->last_cost[1]; if (s->last_cost[2] < c3) c3 = s->last_cost[2];
        int want = (int)ceil(c3 - 0.05);
        if (want < s->k + 1) want = s->k + 1;
        if (want > kmax) want = kmax;
        if (s->trial || (s->probe == 2 && s->since < hold_max)) { s->failed++; s->trial = 0; s->hold = s->hold * 2 < hold_max ? s->hold * 2 : hold_max; }
        else if (s->probe == 2) s->hold = hold0;   // the probe's run at kmin lasted
        if (held == kmin && s->run >= hold_max) s->cref = s->crun;   // kmin held 8 s at this cost
        s->k = want; s->ups++; s->late_run = s->fit_run = 0; s->since = 0; s->probe = 0;
    } else if (s->trial && !grace && !--s->trial) { if (s->probe) { s->probe = 2; s->since = 0; } else s->hold = hold0; }   // the trial held (a probe's run at kmin is judged at the next step up)
    // A frame also fits k − 1 while the running mean of this hold's frames on time does: single frames over the fit among frames under it are
    // what the shorter hold absorbs, and they kept the trial from ever starting (Ocarina of Time on a Mac after a load's late frames: 13.4 ms of GPU work at hold 2 with one
    // frame in 20 over 14.2 ms, 30 fps for the rest of the scene where 60 had held; 22 ms at hold 3 under a lowered GPU clock with frames of 29–44 ms, 20 fps for 25 s)
    double fitc = s->ck == s->k && s->cn && s->ccur < cost ? s->ccur : cost;
    if (!late) s->fit_run = s->k > kmin && fitc <= FSTEP_FIT * (s->k - 1) ? s->fit_run + 1 : 0;
    if (s->fit_run >= FSTEP_RUN && s->since >= s->hold && !s->trial) { s->k--; s->downs++; s->trial = FSTEP_RUN; s->fit_run = 0; }
    else if ((slow || nvn_fstep_same(s)) && s->k > kmin && s->since >= s->hold && !s->trial) {   // probe: straight to kmin, so the controller sees the whole deadline
        s->k = kmin; s->downs++; s->probes++; s->trial = FSTEP_RUN; s->probe = 1; s->grace = FSTEP_GRACE; s->fit_run = s->late_run = 0; s->pa = s->pb = 0; s->plate = s->ptotal = 0;
    }
    s->step = s->k + (s->debt >= 1 && s->k < smax);
    s->paid += s->step > s->k;
    return s->step;
}

// The GPU clock follows the hold too: Breath of the Wild on an iPhone went from 14.4 to about 25 ms of GPU time a frame at hold 2 with the same 4,900 draws, the CPU still on its
// performance cores, so its cost never fitted hold 1 again. The GPU counts as slowed (another reason for nvn_fstep_next's slow) when its time at a hold above kmin is at least
// FSTEP_GPU_SLOW times its time at kmin and it alone does not fit k − 1 (a GPU at 3 ms of 17, 6 times its time on a loading screen, is not what holds a frame back).
// The reference is not updated during a probe's trial (its frames run while the clock is still rising), so a failed probe leaves it as it was. It is kept for each kmin: one
// learned at a 30 fps cap is the GPU time at the clock that cap left (lowered for 30 fps, and under the thermal cap for the heat), and taken as hold 1's after the cap rose it
// made the same work at hold 2 look not slowed
#define FSTEP_GPU_SLOW 1.3    // GPU time at the longer hold against its time at kmin
#define FSTEP_GPU_N 30        // frames at the longer hold before the comparison counts
typedef struct { double ref, cur; int n, k; double ref_at[FSTEP_MAX + 1]; } nvn_fgpu;   // GPU time at kmin (running mean; of every kmin in ref_at); at the current hold k and its frame count
static inline int nvn_fgpu_slow(const nvn_fgpu *g) { return g->n >= FSTEP_GPU_N && g->ref > 0 && g->cur >= FSTEP_GPU_SLOW * g->ref && g->cur > FSTEP_FIT * (g->k - 1); }
// Once per frame, with the frame's GPU time (vsyncs; 0 = none finished yet) and the hold and probe state (nvn_fstep.probe) it ran under
static inline int nvn_fstep_gpu_slowed(nvn_fgpu *g, double gpu, int k, int kmin, int probe) {
    if (kmin < 1 || kmin > FSTEP_MAX) return 0;   // no reference slot for it (hle_nvn.c passes 1 or 2)
    g->ref = g->ref_at[kmin];
    if (gpu <= 0) return nvn_fgpu_slow(g);
    if (k <= kmin) { if (probe != 1) g->ref = g->ref_at[kmin] = g->ref > 0 ? g->ref + (gpu - g->ref) / 32 : gpu; g->n = 0; g->k = k; return 0; }
    if (k != g->k) { g->k = k; g->n = 0; }
    g->cur = g->n ? g->cur + (gpu - g->cur) / 8 : gpu; g->n++;
    return nvn_fgpu_slow(g);
}


########## 8. FPS lock e configurazione host ##########

// Engine frame limits kept in game memory (FPSLocker's evaluate_write entries): some engines cap their own frame rate with a value the host can raise. The target is the profile's
// fps_target (DM_FPS_TARGET overrides; 0 = leave the game's own limit), the same key that drives Tears of the Kingdom's frame step (loader.c install_fps_state). Called on every present
// (hle_nvn.c); the game sets the values after boot and may set them again, so each is written whenever it differs. Fixed addresses: each row runs only on the main build it was found in (AGENTS.md).
// A target frame rate the game steps by needs no row either: the rewriter finds it by its readers in any build (dm/tools/fps_target.py, main's fixups FPS_TARGET_PTR / FPS_TARGET_FIELD).
// Nor do Unity's Application.targetFrameRate and QualitySettings.vSyncCount: the rewriter finds them through the engine's internal-call table (dm/tools/unity_fps.py, main's fixups UNITY_*).
// Unreal Engine needs no row: the rewriter finds its console variables by their registered names in any build (dm/tools/ue_cvar.py, main's fixups UE_CVAR:<name>), and the host writes
// the frame limit, the profile's ue_fps_cvar (t.MaxFPS, or a game's own variable its settings apply to t.MaxFPS: SHIN MEGAMI TENSEI V: Vengeance's Project.FrameRateLimit), and the
// present interval, rhi.SyncInterval (nvn.SyncInterval in UE 4.18's Switch RHI: DRAGON QUEST XI S). Each is a TAutoConsoleVariable whose +0x10 points to its value, the game thread's
// copy then the render thread's. The games' configs set the limit to 30 and the interval to 2 (their notes name the .ini files). An engine with a fixed frame rate (bUseFixedFrameRate) steps
// by and holds to UEngine::FixedFrameRate instead, which the rewriter finds through its reflection entry and GEngine where the engine is made (dm/tools/ue_fixed_rate.py, main's fixups
// UE_FIXED_RATE_PTR / _FIELD / _FLAG): DRAGON BALL: Sparking! ZERO's battles and Pikmin 4. It is written only while the object's bUseFixedFrameRate is set (_FLAG), so an engine stepping by
// the time that passed is left as it is
#include "hle.h"
#include <mach/mach.h>

// What a field holds: the frame rate as a float, double or int32, vsyncs per frame (60 / frame rate) as an int32, or the frame time in milliseconds as a float. Copies: consecutive copies of the
// value (Unreal keeps one for the game thread, one for the render thread). A row with no pointer (ptr_off 0) has its field at main + field: a constant in main's read-only data, which the loader
// leaves writable (the image's data block on iOS too, loader.c map_image).
// At 60 a frame time gets MS_MARGIN less than the vsync: such a limiter counts from the frame's start, and the work after it (the GPU fence wait, the next frame's start) adds to the
// period, so frames at exactly 16.667 ms came 0.11 ms late each on the Mac (59.6 fps, every 150th frame shown two vsyncs). Slightly shorter, the host's present pacing sets the pace
// (the acquire waits): Luigi's Mansion 3's display interval p99 18.69 → 16.67 ms, 60.0 fps. Not at 30: with present_interval display the presents follow every vsync and hold no
// frame for two, so a shorter time showed some frames for one (30.4 fps); 30 writes the game's own 33.333 ms
// Also: a frame time in ticks as a uint32 (scale / frame rate: 19,200,000 for the Switch's 19.2 MHz system tick), a frame step in seconds as a float (1 / frame rate), and a mode
// switch an engine reads before it takes those fields at all (written 1 at any target)
enum { FPS_F32, VSYNCS_I32, MS_F32, FPS_I32, TICKS_U32, SECS_F32, MODE_U32, FPS_F64 };
#define MS_MARGIN 0.5f
static float ms_want(int fps) { return 1000.0f / (float)fps - (fps == 60 ? MS_MARGIN : 0); }
typedef struct { const char *build, *what; uint64_t ptr_off; uint32_t field; uint8_t kind, copies; uint32_t scale; uint32_t flag; } lock_t;   // flag: byte offset << 8 | bit mask the object must have set for the write (0: none)
static const lock_t k_locks[] = {
    // Monster Hunter Rise 16.0.2: RE Engine's frame limit, a float at [main+0x1295b3f0]+0x434 (the pointer is a global in main's bss). The frame loop (main+0x6b106c8) sleeps until
    // [+0x430] / [+0x434] sixtieths of a second have passed ([+0x430] = 60) and steps the game by the time that really passed (+0x41c), so a higher limit runs the game faster in frames
    // at the same speed. The game sets 30 after boot; it also asks for present interval 2, which the profile's present_interval display ignores.
    // From masagrator's FPSLocker config for this build (FPSLocker-Warehouse, patches/0100B04011742000/C9A3DD7702075ECD.yaml)
    { "c9a3dd7702075ecd90101f4555389582", "RE Engine frame limit", 0x1295b3f0, 0x434, FPS_F32, 1 },
    // Resident Evil HD Remaster 1.0.0: timing probe. The constructor initializes adjacent floats at +0x48 and +0x4c to 30.0;
    // sMain::move reads both (main+0x775b34 and main+0x775b94). Keep the pair synchronized while testing the MT Framework limit.
    { "6bec9b23b09df46c315aa6f4bfacf91c", "Resident Evil MT Framework primary frame limit", 0x157daa0, 0x48, FPS_F32, 2 },
    // Luigi's Mansion 3 1.4.0: Next Level Games' frame limiter. At the end of each frame the main thread calls the frame callbacks (main+0xb7c308) with the milliseconds since the frame
    // started; the limiter (main+0x7a3e70) runs jobs or sleeps until 33.333 ms have passed, the float at main+0x13c94dc (read only there, at main+0x7a3ea8 and main+0x7a3f18), and the game
    // steps by the time that really passed. The game asks for present interval 2 too, which the profile's present_interval display ignores; both are needed
    { "79e5950ffa85acf63e28c9aec051eac2", "NLG frame limiter target", 0, 0x13c94dc, MS_F32, 1 },
    // Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered 1.0.3: Criterion's frame timing. A uint32 in main's bss (main+0xf0043c) selects the engine's 60 fps mode, in which it takes its frame time from
    // the timer object at [main+0xed96a8]: +0x30 the frame in system ticks (19.2 MHz, 640,000 at 30 fps) and +0x28 a tenth of it; the game's own step, at [main+0xeffc60] +0x30 (2D) and +0x50
    // (3D), is a float of seconds per frame. Its limiter, a spin on the system tick at main+0x483588..+0x4835a4, is cut by the rewriter (patches.py). From masagrator's FPSLocker config for this
    // build (FPSLocker-Warehouse, patches/010029B0118E8000/799D1061182C1302.yaml; the frame-time instruction found by theboy181)
    { "799d1061182c1302e08e706b84ce76e5", "Criterion 60 fps mode", 0, 0xf0043c, MODE_U32, 1, 0 },
    { "799d1061182c1302e08e706b84ce76e5", "Criterion frame ticks", 0xed96a8, 0x30, TICKS_U32, 1, 19200000 },
    { "799d1061182c1302e08e706b84ce76e5", "Criterion frame ticks / 10", 0xed96a8, 0x28, TICKS_U32, 1, 1920000 },
    { "799d1061182c1302e08e706b84ce76e5", "Criterion 2D game step", 0xeffc60, 0x30, SECS_F32, 1, 0 },
    { "799d1061182c1302e08e706b84ce76e5", "Criterion 3D game step", 0xeffc60, 0x50, SECS_F32, 1, 0 },
    // EA SPORTS FC 27 1.8d.310c: the game's frame regulator, an object at [main+0xda20e38] (its constructor, main+0x99e80c8, sets 60.0). Its tick (main+0x99ea580) waits until
    // 1 / [+0x8] seconds have passed since the last frame; [+0x10] is the rate it reports. main+0x5d501c0 sets both to 30.0 whenever GameRenderSettings.Enable is 1 (fmov v1.2d, #30.0;
    // stur q1, [x9, #8]), a constant of the Switch build, so it is written here. The simulation's own rate is Frostbite's SimulationTimeSettings, set below by name: on a build without
    // this row the game keeps 30 fps at the right speed (the simulation at 60 and the regulator at 30: match clock as at 30). The game asks for present interval 2

    { "a48c0de3bc353efa0e4d359bde05ef24", "FIFA frame regulator", 0xda20e38, 0x8, FPS_F64, 2, 0 },

#define NLOCKS ((int)(sizeof k_locks / sizeof k_locks[0]))

static int rd(uint64_t a, void *out, size_t n) { vm_size_t got = 0; return a >= 0x1000 && vm_read_overwrite(mach_task_self(), (vm_address_t)a, n, (vm_address_t)out, &got) == KERN_SUCCESS && got == n; }

// Resident Evil 0 1.0.0: read-only check of the MT Framework timing value used by
// sRender::end (main+0x1285650 -> object1 -> object2+0x48). The addresses were
// identified in the surveyed executable; do not turn this into a write row until
// the live pointer chain and value have been confirmed on device.
static void re0_timing_probe(void) {
    static int done, tries;
    if (done) return;
    module_t *m = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmod; i++)
        if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].name, "main") &&
            !strcmp(g_mod[i].build_id, "fb4239aa962b429b3d1776af92d93e79")) {
            m = &g_mod[i];
            break;
        }
    if (!m) { if (++tries >= 600) { FILE *pf = fopen("/tmp/re0_timing_probe.log", "w"); if (pf) { fputs("main module with the surveyed RE0 build ID was not found\n", pf); fclose(pf); } done = 1; } return; }
    const uint64_t slot_off = 0x1285650;
    if (slot_off > m->size || m->size - slot_off < sizeof(uint64_t)) {
        LOG("[RE0 timing probe] main image is too small for the surveyed timing slot");
        done = 1;
        return;
    }
    uint64_t object1 = 0, object2 = 0;
    uint32_t raw = 0;
    uint64_t slot = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(m->base + slot_off);
    if (!rd(slot, &object1, sizeof object1) || object1 < 0x1000 ||
        !rd(object1, &object2, sizeof object2) || object2 < 0x1000 ||
        object2 > UINT64_MAX - 0x48 ||
        !rd(object2 + 0x48, &raw, sizeof raw)) {
        if (++tries >= 600) {
            LOG("[RE0 timing probe] timing pointer chain not readable after %d presents; no memory written", tries);
            FILE *pf = fopen("/tmp/re0_timing_probe.log", "w"); if (pf) { fprintf(pf, "pointer chain unreadable after %d presents\n", tries); fclose(pf); }
            done = 1;
        }
        return;
    }
    float fps;
    memcpy(&fps, &raw, sizeof fps);
    if (!(fps >= 10.0f && fps <= 120.0f)) {
        if (++tries >= 600) {
            LOG("[RE0 timing probe] object chain readable but +0x48 is not a plausible FPS value (bits=%08x); no memory written", raw);
            FILE *pf = fopen("/tmp/re0_timing_probe.log", "w"); if (pf) { fprintf(pf, "object chain readable; +0x48 bits=%08x is outside 10..120 FPS\n", raw); fclose(pf); }
            done = 1;
        }
        return;
    }
    FILE *pf = fopen("/tmp/re0_timing_probe.log", "w");
    if (pf) {
        fprintf(pf, "build=fb4239aa962b429b3d1776af92d93e79\nslot=main+%#llx\nobject1=%p\nobject2=%p\nobject2+0x48=%g fps (bits=%08x)\n",
                (unsigned long long)slot_off, (void *)(uintptr_t)object1,
                (void *)(uintptr_t)object2, fps, raw);
        fclose(pf);
    }
    LOG("[RE0 timing probe] live MT timing chain verified: main+%#llx -> %p -> %p, +0x48=%g fps; read-only",
        (unsigned long long)slot_off, (void *)(uintptr_t)object1,
        (void *)(uintptr_t)object2, fps);
    done = 1;
}

// EXPERIMENTAL, intentionally unsafe RE0 timing-field test. This is opt-in only:
// DM_RE0_UNSAFE_TIMING=1 plus DM_FPS_TARGET=60 or 120. The field is known to
// participate in MT Framework time scaling, but is NOT proven to be an FPS
// selector; this test may change simulation speed. Build-ID and pointer/value
// guards keep it confined to the surveyed RE0 1.0.0 process.
static module_t *re0_unsafe_main(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmod; i++)
        if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].name, "main") &&
            !strcmp(g_mod[i].build_id, "fb4239aa962b429b3d1776af92d93e79"))
            return &g_mod[i];
    return NULL;
}
static int re0_unsafe_enabled(void) {
    // Disabled after device testing showed that these MT Framework fields scale
    // simulation speed as well as frame pacing. Do not write them for RE0.
    return 0;
}
static void re0_unsafe_tick(int target, const char *src) {
    static int nlog;
    module_t *m = re0_unsafe_main();
    if (!m || (target != 60 && target != 120) || 0x1285650 > m->size ||
        m->size - 0x1285650 < sizeof(uint64_t)) return;
    uint64_t object1 = 0, object2 = 0;
    if (!rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(m->base + 0x1285650), &object1, sizeof object1) ||
        object1 < 0x1000 ||
        !rd(object1, &object2, sizeof object2) || object2 < 0x1000 ||
        object2 > UINT64_MAX - 0x48) return;
    uint32_t cur;
    if (!rd(object2 + 0x48, &cur, sizeof cur)) return;
    float value; memcpy(&value, &cur, sizeof value);
    if (!(value >= 10.0f && value <= 120.0f)) return;
    if (value == (float)target) return;
    float want_f = (float)target; uint32_t want;
    memcpy(&want, &want_f, sizeof want);
    uint32_t *p = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(object2 + 0x48);
    dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p);
    __atomic_store_n(p, want, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (nlog++ < 16)
        LOG("[RE0 UNSAFE TEST] object2+0x48 %.3f → %d (DM_RE0_UNSAFE_TIMING=1; %s); simulation speed may change",
            value, target, src);
}

// NieR 1.0.3 exposes its preset minimum but ships fixed mode-specific fallbacks.
// Keep the native current-scale and UV controller intact; only select its
// verified lower bound. This is independent of the FPS choice.
// The 1.0.3 builds the rewrite cuts (patches.py): the scale clamp and the publish branch that are checked, the two fallback floors the cuts
// replace, and the preset minimum. The Asian release (0100B8E016F76000) shifts the function by 0x13c0; its preset minimum is the target of the
// relocation of the slot the function loads it through (main+0x12c8500).
// display is the game's display object: its first word points to the NVN device (the present interval at +0x9c160), and +0x504 is the frame-interval
// mode (0: 60 fps, 1: 30 fps) the setter main+0x9c0590 (Asian release; the global's 0x13c0 before) writes; in the Asian release it is the target of the
// relocation of the slot that setter reads (main+0x12c2d18).
static const struct { const char *build; uint32_t clamp, publish, floor0, floor1, minimum, display; } k_nier_dr[] = {
    {"3c10ec35c5ef4c3686b4053afb0e58e7", 0x9bf568, 0x9bf578, 0x9bf528, 0x9bf534, 0x128e068, 0x192be00},
    {"98397a10419894652f372d4dc1b6fc2c", 0x9c0928, 0x9c0938, 0x9c08e8, 0x9c08f4, 0x128f130, 0x192d600},
};
static void dynamic_resolution_tick(void) {
    static int state = -1, dynamic, row;
    static uint8_t *base;
    if (state < 0) {
        state = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < g_nmod; i++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].name, "main"))
            for (int k = 0; k < (int)(sizeof k_nier_dr / sizeof *k_nier_dr); k++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].build_id, k_nier_dr[k].build)) { base = g_mod[i].base; row = k; }
        if (!base) return;
        const char *e=getenv("DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION");
        if (e && strcmp(e,"0") && strcmp(e,"1")) LOG("[RED] DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=%s: must be 0 or 1; keeping full resolution",e);
        dynamic=e && !strcmp(e,"1");
        if (dynamic) {
            uint32_t clamp = 0, publish = 0;
            uint64_t floors[2] = {0};
            if (!rd((uint64_t)(base + k_nier_dr[row].clamp), &clamp, 4) || !rd((uint64_t)(base + k_nier_dr[row].publish), &publish, 4) ||
                !rd((uint64_t)(base + k_nier_dr[row].floor0), &floors[0], 8) || !rd((uint64_t)(base + k_nier_dr[row].floor1), &floors[1], 8) ||
                clamp != 0x1e254c80u || publish != 0x54000489u ||
                floors[0] != 0x72a7f00c5280000cull || floors[1] != 0x72a7f00c5280000cull) {
                LOG("[RED] dynamic resolution needs a verified native scale/UV rewrite; keeping full resolution");
                dynamic = 0;
            }
        }
        state=1;
        LOG("main: NieR dynamic resolution %s (DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION)",dynamic?"on; native controller, 70–100% scale":"off; full resolution");
    }
    if (!state) return;
    uint32_t cur[2];
    uint64_t a = (uint64_t)(base + k_nier_dr[row].minimum);
    if (!rd(a, cur, sizeof cur)) return;
    uint32_t minimum = dynamic ? 0x3f333333u : 0x3f800000u;
    if (cur[0] != minimum) {
        uint32_t *p = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)a;
        dm_guest_write_prepare(p, 4);
        __atomic_store_n(p, minimum, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
    if (!dynamic && cur[1] != 0x3f800000u) {
        uint32_t *p = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(a + 4);
        dm_guest_write_prepare(p, 4);
        __atomic_store_n(p, 0x3f800000u, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
}

// Frostbite's simulation rate, found by name (no fixed addresses, so it holds across a game's updates). Frostbite reflects its settings classes: a class record (its name, then at
// +0x40 its field list) and per field a record of 0x20 bytes (name, hash, offset at +0x10, type). SimulationTimeSettings' ForceSimRate (int32) and MaxSimFps (float) cap the
// simulation's ticks a second: 30 in EA SPORTS FC 27, whose frames then cannot go faster than 30 whatever paces them. A static constructor registers the class: it stores the record's
// address into its type info (adrp / add of the record, then str into the type info just made by adrp / add), and the code that reads the settings asks the settings registry for the
// instance with that type info in x1 and a cache word in x2 (adrp / add each, then bl), which keeps the instance's address. The instance holds its type info at +8, which checks the cache.
// Both fields are written each frame they differ (the game may load its settings again), like the frame limits above
static struct { int n; uint8_t *base; uint64_t ti, cache[8]; int ncache; uint32_t off_rate, off_max; } fb;
static int fb_name_at(uint8_t *base, uint64_t size, uint64_t p, const char *want) {   // p, a relocated pointer, points into the module at the string want
    uint64_t b = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)base; size_t n = strlen(want);
    return p >= b && p - b + n + 1 <= size && !memcmp((const void *)(uintptr_t)p, want, n + 1);
}
static int64_t fb_pair(const uint32_t *t, uint64_t i, int reg) {   // the target of adrp / add into reg at words i, i + 1, or -1 (module offsets: the text sits at offset 0)
    uint32_t w = t[i], x = t[i + 1];
    if ((w & 0x9F000000u) != 0x90000000u || (int)(w & 31) != reg || (x & 0xFFC00000u) != 0x91000000u || (x & 31) != (uint32_t)reg || ((x >> 5) & 31) != (uint32_t)reg) return -1;
    int64_t imm = (int64_t)(((w >> 29) & 3) | (((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2)); if (imm & (1 << 20)) imm -= 1 << 21;
    return (int64_t)((i * 4) & ~0xfffull) + imm * 4096 + ((x >> 10) & 0xfff);
}
static void fb_find(void) {
    module_t *m = NULL; for (int i = 0; i < g_nmod; i++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].name, "main")) m = &g_mod[i];
    if (!m || !m->text_end || !m->ro_off || m->ro_off >= m->size) return;
    static const char cls[] = "SimulationTimeSettings";
    uint8_t *base = m->base, *ro = base + m->ro_off; uint64_t size = m->back_off ? m->back_off : m->size, b = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)base;
    const uint8_t *s = memmem(ro, (size_t)(size - m->ro_off), "\0SimulationTimeSettings\0", sizeof cls + 1); if (!s) return;   // not Frostbite
    uint64_t name = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(s + 1), rec = 0;
    for (uint64_t o = (m->ro_off + 7) & ~7ull; o + 0x48 <= size && !rec; o += 8) {
        if (*(uint64_t *)(base + o) != name) continue;
        uint64_t fl = *(uint64_t *)(base + o + 0x40); if (fl < b || fl - b + 0x20 > size) continue;
        for (uint64_t f = fl - b; f + 0x20 <= size; f += 0x20) {   // the field list ends where a name stops being one
            uint64_t fn = *(uint64_t *)(base + f); if (fn < b || fn - b >= size) break;
            uint32_t off = *(uint32_t *)(base + f + 0x10);
            if (fb_name_at(base, size, fn, "ForceSimRate")) fb.off_rate = off;
            else if (fb_name_at(base, size, fn, "MaxSimFps")) fb.off_max = off;
        }
        if (fb.off_rate && fb.off_max) rec = o;
    }
    if (!rec) { LOG("[RED] main: Frostbite's %s found, but not its ForceSimRate and MaxSimFps fields; leaving the simulation rate", cls); return; }
    const uint32_t *t = (const uint32_t *)base; uint64_t nw = m->text_end / 4;
    for (uint64_t i = 0; i + 3 < nw && !fb.ti; i++) {   // the registration: adrp / add xR = record, str xR, [xT] with xT = the type info from an adrp / add just before
        int r = (int)(t[i] & 31); if (fb_pair(t, i, r) != (int64_t)rec) continue;
        uint32_t st = t[i + 2]; if ((st & 0xFFFFFC00u) != 0xF9000000u || (int)(st & 31) != r) continue;   // str xR, [xT] (no offset)
        int xt = (int)((st >> 5) & 31);
        for (uint64_t k = i >= 6 ? i - 6 : 0; k < i; k++) { int64_t ti = fb_pair(t, k, xt); if (ti > 0) fb.ti = (uint64_t)ti; }
    }
    if (!fb.ti) { LOG("[RED] main: Frostbite's %s: its type info was not found; leaving the simulation rate", cls); return; }
    for (uint64_t i = 8; i + 12 < nw && fb.ncache < 8; i++) {   // the readers: adrp / add x1 = type info, adrp / add x2 = cache word, near each other before a bl
        if (fb_pair(t, i, 1) != (int64_t)fb.ti) continue;
        for (uint64_t k = i - 8; k < i + 10; k++) {
            int64_t c = fb_pair(t, k, 2); if (c <= 0 || (uint64_t)c + 8 > m->size) continue;
            int known = 0; for (int j = 0; j < fb.ncache; j++) known |= fb.cache[j] == (uint64_t)c;
            if (!known) fb.cache[fb.ncache++] = (uint64_t)c;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!fb.ncache) { LOG("[RED] main: Frostbite's %s: no settings lookup found; leaving the simulation rate", cls); return; }
    fb.base = base; fb.n = 1;
    LOG("main: Frostbite %s at main+%#llx (ForceSimRate +%#x, MaxSimFps +%#x), type info main+%#llx, %d instance caches", cls, (unsigned long long)rec, fb.off_rate, fb.off_max,
        (unsigned long long)fb.ti, fb.ncache);
}
static void fb_tick(int target, const char *src) {
    static int nlog; uint64_t ti = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(fb.base + fb.ti);
    for (int j = 0; j < fb.ncache; j++) {
        uint64_t inst = 0, tinfo = 0; int32_t rate; float max;
        if (!rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(fb.base + fb.cache[j]), &inst, sizeof inst) || !inst || !rd(inst + 8, &tinfo, sizeof tinfo) || tinfo != ti) continue;   // not made yet, or another word
        if (!rd(inst + fb.off_rate, &rate, sizeof rate) || !rd(inst + fb.off_max, &max, sizeof max)) continue;
        if (rate != target) { int32_t *p = (int32_t *)(uintptr_t)(inst + fb.off_rate); dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p); __atomic_store_n(p, target, __ATOMIC_RELAXED); }
        if (max != (float)target) { float w = (float)target, *p = (float *)(uintptr_t)(inst + fb.off_max); dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p); __atomic_store_n((uint32_t *)p, *(uint32_t *)&w, __ATOMIC_RELAXED); }
        if ((rate != target || max != (float)target) && nlog < 8) { nlog++; LOG("main: Frostbite simulation rate ForceSimRate %d, MaxSimFps %g → %d (%s)", rate, max, target, src); }
        return;
    }
}

// The row of a target frame rate the game steps by, at the place the rewriter found (dm/tools/fps_target.py; main's fixups FPS_TARGET_PTR, FPS_TARGET_FIELD): an int32 frame rate in the
// object a global points to, which the game's readers divide 60.0 by to step it, and which the game sets to 30 or 60 itself. Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave's gxc graphics object holds it
// (+0x1dc; its present asks for interval 60 / target), so at 60 the game asks for interval 1 and steps by 1.0 a frame. 0 rows: not found in this main
static int target_row(const module_t *m, lock_t *out) {
    if (!m->fps_target_ptr) return 0;
    *out = (lock_t){ "", "target frame rate", m->fps_target_ptr, m->fps_target_field, FPS_I32, 1, 0 };
    return 1;
}

// The Unreal rows of this main: the profile's frame-limit variable and the present intervals, at the objects the rewriter found, and the engine's fixed frame rate on GEngine (0 rows:
// not an Unreal main). *missing: an Unreal main (the rewriter found some of its variables) without the profile's frame-limit variable
static int ue_rows(const module_t *m, lock_t *out, int *missing) {
    static char what[4][48]; int n = 0, have = 0;
    if (m->ue_fixed_ptr && m->ue_fixed_flag) out[n++] = (lock_t){ "", "Unreal fixed frame rate (GEngine->FixedFrameRate)", m->ue_fixed_ptr, m->ue_fixed_field, FPS_F32, 1, 0, m->ue_fixed_flag };
    for (int k = 0; k < m->n_ue_cvar && n < 4; k++) {
        const char *name = m->ue_cvar[k].name; int fps = !strcmp(name, DM_GAME_UE_FPS_CVAR);
        if (!fps && strcmp(name, "rhi.SyncInterval") && strcmp(name, "nvn.SyncInterval")) continue;
        have |= fps; snprintf(what[n], sizeof what[n], "Unreal %s", name);
        out[n] = (lock_t){ "", what[n], m->ue_cvar[k].off + 0x10, 0, fps ? FPS_F32 : VSYNCS_I32, 2, 0 }; n++;
    }
    *missing = m->n_ue_cvar > 0 && !have;
    return n;
}

// Unity's frame rate, at the places the rewriter found through the engine's internal-call table (dm/tools/unity_fps.py; main's fixups UNITY_*), in any Unity build it reads:
// Application.targetFrameRate, an int32 in main's bss (-1 until a game sets it: left so), and the current quality level's vSyncCount. On the Switch, Unity presents at
// vSyncCount vsyncs a frame: QualitySettings.vSyncCount's setter hands the count to the graphics device, which calls nvnWindowSetPresentInterval when it changes, and Unity steps
// the game by the time that really passed (The Rogue Prince of Persia: vSyncCount 2, targetFrameRate -1; the same walk covers the same ground at 30 and 60 fps). The device
// takes the count only through the setter, so writing the level's count does not change the interval the game asks for: the host's present cap does (hle_nvn.c), as for
// every engine limit here; the write keeps what the game reads back (QualitySettings.vSyncCount) the same as what it shows
static struct { uint8_t *base; uint64_t ptr; uint32_t idx, arr, size, vsync; } uq;
static void unity_vsync_tick(int target, const char *src) {
    static int nlog; uint64_t obj = 0, arr = 0; int32_t lvl; uint32_t cur, want = target > 60 ? 1 : 60 / (uint32_t)target;
    if (!rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(uq.base + uq.ptr), &obj, sizeof obj) || !obj) return;   // not made yet
    if (!rd(obj + uq.idx, &lvl, sizeof lvl) || lvl < 0 || lvl > 64 || !rd(obj + uq.arr, &arr, sizeof arr) || !arr) return;
    uint64_t a = arr + (uint64_t)lvl * uq.size + uq.vsync;
    if (!rd(a, &cur, sizeof cur) || cur == want || cur < 1 || cur > 4) return;   // already set, or 0: the game paces by targetFrameRate instead
    uint32_t *p = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)a; dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p); __atomic_store_n(p, want, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (nlog < 8) { nlog++; LOG("main: Unity QualitySettings.vSyncCount (level %d) %u → %u vsyncs (%d fps; %s)", lvl, cur, want, target, src); }
}
// The running main's engine limiters, found once: by the first present (dm_fps_lock_tick) or by the graphics layer's present cap, which may ask first (dm_fps_lock_engine, from the acquire)
static lock_t ue[4], target_lock, unity_tfr; static const lock_t *rows[NLOCKS + 6]; static int nrow, nier, ue_missing; static uint8_t *base; static uint32_t display;
static pthread_once_t g_found = PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT;
static void lock_find(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmod; i++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].name, "main")) {
        for (int k = 0; k < (int)(sizeof k_nier_dr / sizeof *k_nier_dr); k++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].build_id, k_nier_dr[k].build)) { base = g_mod[i].base; nier = 1; display = k_nier_dr[k].display; }
        for (int k = 0; k < NLOCKS; k++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].build_id, k_locks[k].build)) { rows[nrow++] = &k_locks[k]; base = g_mod[i].base; }
        if (target_row(&g_mod[i], &target_lock)) { rows[nrow++] = &target_lock; base = g_mod[i].base; }
        int nue = ue_rows(&g_mod[i], ue, &ue_missing);
        for (int k = 0; k < nue; k++) { rows[nrow++] = &ue[k]; base = g_mod[i].base; }
        if (g_mod[i].unity_target_fps) {   // unless a build row writes the same field
            int dup = 0; for (int r = 0; r < nrow; r++) dup |= !rows[r]->ptr_off && rows[r]->field == (uint32_t)g_mod[i].unity_target_fps;
            unity_tfr = (lock_t){ "", "Unity Application.targetFrameRate", 0, (uint32_t)g_mod[i].unity_target_fps, FPS_I32, 1, 0 };
            if (!dup) { rows[nrow++] = &unity_tfr; base = g_mod[i].base; }
        }
        if (g_mod[i].unity_qs_ptr && g_mod[i].unity_qs_size) {
            uq.base = g_mod[i].base; uq.ptr = g_mod[i].unity_qs_ptr; uq.idx = g_mod[i].unity_qs_idx; uq.arr = g_mod[i].unity_qs_arr; uq.size = g_mod[i].unity_qs_size; uq.vsync = g_mod[i].unity_qs_vsync;
            LOG("main: Unity QualitySettings at [main+%#llx], vSyncCount at [+%#x] + [+%#x] * %#x + %#x", (unsigned long long)uq.ptr, uq.arr, uq.idx, uq.size, uq.vsync);
        }
    }
    fb_find();
}
// Whether the host writes fps_target into an engine limiter of this main (a row for its build, NieR's frame interval, a target frame rate found by its readers, Unreal's variables or
// Frostbite's simulation rate, found by name).
// Without one, and without a frame step state page, nothing makes the game follow the cap, so the graphics layer keeps the game's own present interval (hle_nvn.c fps_present_cap):
// presenting at a cap the game does not step by runs a fixed-step game fast or slow (Tears of the Kingdom 1.4.2 at 2x with DM_FPS_TARGET=60)
int dm_fps_lock_engine(void) { pthread_once(&g_found, lock_find); return nrow || nier || fb.n || uq.base || re0_unsafe_enabled(); }
int nvn_fps_high_now(void);   // hle_nvn.c
int nvn_game_fps(void);       // hle_nvn.c: sustained game-requested 30 fps interval
void dm_fps_lock_tick(void) {
    re0_timing_probe();       // RE0: verify its live timing pointer chain without writing guest memory
    dynamic_resolution_tick();   // separate from the FPS cap
    static int state = -2, nlog[NLOCKS + 5], target, high; static const char *src;
    if (state == -1) return;
    if (state == -2) {
        state = -1; pthread_once(&g_found, lock_find);
        if (!nrow && !nier && !fb.n && !uq.base && !ue_missing && !re0_unsafe_enabled()) return;
        const char *e = getenv("DM_FPS_TARGET"); int t = e ? atoi(e) : DM_GAME_FPS_TARGET; src = e ? "DM_FPS_TARGET" : "game profile fps_target";
        if (t != 0 && t != 30 && t != 60 && t != 120) { LOG("[RED] DM_FPS_TARGET=%s: must be 0, 30, 60 or 120; leaving the game's frame limit", e); t = 0; }
        if (t == 120 && DM_GAME_FPS_MAX < 120) { LOG("[RED] DM_FPS_TARGET=120: this game's speed at 120 fps is not checked (profile fps_max); running at 60"); t = 60; }
        high = t == 120;
        if (t && ue_missing) LOG("[RED] main: Unreal %s not found by the rewriter (ue_cvar.py NAMES; game profile ue_fps_cvar): the game's own frame limit stays", DM_GAME_UE_FPS_CVAR);
        if (!nrow && !nier && !fb.n && !uq.base && !re0_unsafe_enabled()) return;
        if (!t) { for (int r = 0; r < nrow; r++) LOG("main: %s left as the game sets it (%s)", rows[r]->what, src); if (nier) LOG("main: NieR frame interval left as the game sets it (%s)", src);
                  if (fb.n) LOG("main: Frostbite simulation rate left as the game sets it (%s)", src); if (uq.base) LOG("main: Unity vSyncCount left as the game sets it (%s)", src); return; }
        target = t; state = 0;
    }
    if (high) target = nvn_fps_high_now();   // only a requested 120 fps target follows the dynamic 120/60 hold
    if (re0_unsafe_enabled()) re0_unsafe_tick(target, src);
    if (nier) {
        // NieR:Automata US/EU 1.0.3 (3c10ec35c5ef4c3686b4053afb0e58e7):
        // - [base + 0x192be00] points to the NVN graphics device object whose +0x9c160 holds the present interval (1 = 60 FPS, 2 = 30 FPS),
        //   and base + 0x192c304 (+0x504) holds the requested interval mode (0 = 60 FPS, 1 = 30 FPS).
        // Resolution policy is applied independently above, so 30/60 FPS does
        // not implicitly enable or disable the native resolution controller.
        uint64_t p = 0; static int nlog_nier;
        uint32_t want = target > 60 ? 1 : (uint32_t)(60 / target), want_mode = want - 1, cur_mode = 0;
        if (rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(base + display + 0x504), &cur_mode, sizeof cur_mode) && cur_mode != want_mode && (cur_mode == 0 || cur_mode == 1)) {
            uint32_t *dst = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(base + display + 0x504);
            dm_guest_write_prepare(dst, sizeof *dst);
            __atomic_store_n(dst, want_mode, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
        }
        if (rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(base + display), &p, sizeof p) && p) {
            uint64_t a = p + 0x9c160; uint32_t cur = 0;
            if (rd(a, &cur, sizeof cur) && cur != want && (cur == 1 || cur == 2)) {
                uint32_t *dst = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)a;
                dm_guest_write_prepare(dst, sizeof *dst); __atomic_store_n(dst, want, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
                if (nlog_nier++ < 8) LOG("main: NieR frame interval %u → %u (%d fps; %s)", cur, want, target, src);
            }
        }
    }
    if (fb.n) fb_tick(target, src);
    if (uq.base) unity_vsync_tick(target, src);
    for (int r = 0; r < nrow; r++) {
        const lock_t *L = rows[r]; uint64_t obj = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)base;
        // Resident Evil: keep MT Framework's game clock in step with the actual
        // movie decoder rate (30 or 60 Hz), regardless of the selected 60/120 fps
        // profile. Outside movies, follow the selected profile; the 120 fps profile
        // continues to follow the display's dynamic 120/60 hold.
        int movie_hz = dm_movie_hz();
        int re_row = !strcmp(L->what, "Resident Evil MT Framework primary frame limit");
        int re0_row = !strcmp(L->what, "Resident Evil 0 experimental timing-rate pair");
        int re_movie = !strcmp(DM_GAME_ID, "010050F00BC1A000") && re_row && movie_hz != 0;
        int row_target = re_movie ? movie_hz : re_row ? nvn_game_fps() : target;
        // The macOS launcher may detach dmhost from the launching terminal, so stderr is
        // not a reliable way to retrieve this one-off investigation. Keep a small,
        // explicit diagnostic file in /tmp, independent of the app's working directory.
        if (re_row) {
            static int probe_file_started;
            if (!probe_file_started) {
                FILE *pf = fopen("/tmp/re_movie_clock_probe.log", "w");
                if (pf) {
                    fprintf(pf, "[RE movie clock probe] FPS-lock tick reached; target=%d, movie_hz=%d\n", target, movie_hz);
                    fclose(pf);
                    probe_file_started = 1;
                }
            }
        }
        if (L->ptr_off && (!rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(base + L->ptr_off), &obj, sizeof obj) || !obj)) continue;   // not created yet
        if (L->flag) { uint8_t b; if (!rd(obj + (L->flag >> 8), &b, 1) || !(b & (L->flag & 0xff))) continue; }   // the object's flag is off (Unreal: no fixed frame rate in use)
        // Resident Evil: the ELF reads the timing fields through two pointer
        // indirections: [main + 0x157daa0] -> object -> timing object.
        // The earlier probe stopped at the first object (whose +0x48/+0x4c
        // are small integer fields), so inspect the second object instead.
        if (re_row) {
            static int baseline_samples, movie_samples;
            if (baseline_samples < 4 || (movie_hz && movie_samples < 8)) {
                uint32_t slot_words[4] = {0}, first_words[4] = {0}, mem[64] = {0};
                uint64_t obj2 = 0;
                int have_slot = rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(base + L->ptr_off), slot_words, sizeof slot_words);
                int have_obj2 = rd(obj, &obj2, sizeof obj2) && obj2 >= 0x1000;
                int have_mem = have_obj2 && rd(obj2, mem, sizeof mem);
                float at48 = 0.0f, at78 = 0.0f;
                if (have_obj2) {
                    uint32_t raw48 = 0, raw78 = 0;
                    if (rd(obj2 + 0x48, &raw48, sizeof raw48)) memcpy(&at48, &raw48, sizeof at48);
                    if (rd(obj2 + 0x78, &raw78, sizeof raw78)) memcpy(&at78, &raw78, sizeof at78);
                }
                rd(obj, first_words, sizeof first_words);
                FILE *pf = fopen("/tmp/re_movie_clock_probe.log", "a");
                if (pf) {
                    fprintf(pf, "[RE MT double] slot=%p object1=%p object2=%p movie_hz=%d target=%d row_target=%d slot_read=%d slot_raw=%08x,%08x,%08x,%08x first_raw=%08x,%08x,%08x,%08x second_raw=%s",
                        (void *)(uintptr_t)(base + L->ptr_off), (void *)(uintptr_t)obj,
                        (void *)(uintptr_t)obj2, movie_hz, target, row_target, have_slot,
                        slot_words[0], slot_words[1], slot_words[2], slot_words[3],
                        first_words[0], first_words[1], first_words[2], first_words[3],
                        have_mem ? "" : "(unreadable)");
                    if (have_mem) {
                        for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) fprintf(pf, "%s%08x", i ? "," : "", mem[i]);
                        fprintf(pf, " float_candidates=");
                        int found = 0;
                        for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
                            float x; memcpy(&x, &mem[i], sizeof x);
                            if (x >= 0.001f && x <= 10000.0f) {
                                fprintf(pf, "%s+%03x:%g", found ? "," : "", i * 4, x);
                                found++;
                            }
                        }
                        if (!found) fprintf(pf, "none");
                    }
                    fprintf(pf, " second_+48=%g second_+78=%g\n", at48, at78);
                    fclose(pf);
                }
                if (movie_hz) movie_samples++; else baseline_samples++;
            }
        }
        // Resident Evil timing fields are in the second object: [main + slot] -> object1 -> timing object.
        // Both RE HD Remaster and RE0 need the extra dereference before writing +0x48/+0x4c.
        if (re_row || re0_row) {
            uint64_t timing_obj = 0;
            if (!rd(obj, &timing_obj, sizeof timing_obj) || timing_obj < 0x1000) continue;
            obj = timing_obj;
        }
        if (L->kind == FPS_F64) {
            for (int c = 0; c < L->copies; c++) {
                uint64_t a = obj + L->field + 8 * (uint64_t)c; double cur, want = row_target;
                if (!rd(a, &cur, sizeof cur)) break;
                if (cur == want || !(cur >= 10 && cur <= 120)) continue;   // already set, or not set yet
                double *p = (double *)(uintptr_t)a;
                dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p); __atomic_store_n((uint64_t *)p, *(uint64_t *)&want, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
                if (nlog[r] < 8) { nlog[r]++; LOG("main: %s%s %g → %d fps (%s)", L->what, L->copies > 1 ? (c ? " (reported rate)" : " (target)") : "", cur, row_target, src); }
            }
            continue;
        }
        for (int c = 0; c < L->copies; c++) {
            uint64_t a = obj + L->field + 4 * (uint64_t)c; uint32_t cur, want; char was[16];
            if (!rd(a, &cur, sizeof cur)) break;
            if (L->kind == FPS_F32 || L->kind == MS_F32) {
                int ms = L->kind == MS_F32; float f, w = ms ? ms_want(row_target) : (float)row_target; memcpy(&f, &cur, sizeof f); memcpy(&want, &w, sizeof want);
                if (cur == want || !(ms ? f >= 8 && f <= 100 : f >= 10 && f <= 120)) continue;   // already set, or not set yet (RE Engine: 6000 at boot; Unreal: 0 = no limit until the config sets it)
                snprintf(was, sizeof was, ms ? "%.3f ms" : "%g", f);
            } else if (L->kind == SECS_F32) {
                float f, w = 1.0f / (float)row_target; memcpy(&f, &cur, sizeof f); memcpy(&want, &w, sizeof want);
                if (cur == want || !(f >= 1.0f / 120 && f <= 0.1f)) continue;   // not set yet (0 before the game's first frame)
                snprintf(was, sizeof was, "%.5f s", f);
            } else if (L->kind == TICKS_U32) {
                want = L->scale / (uint32_t)row_target;
                if (cur == want || cur < L->scale / 120 || cur > L->scale / 10) continue;
                snprintf(was, sizeof was, "%u", cur);
            } else if (L->kind == MODE_U32) {
                want = 1;
                if (cur) continue;   // already 1, or not this switch: 0 is the engine's default
                snprintf(was, sizeof was, "%u", cur);
            } else {
                int fps = L->kind == FPS_I32;
                want = fps ? (uint32_t)row_target : row_target > 60 ? 1 : 60 / (uint32_t)row_target;   // above 60 the display link paces it: a vsync count stays 1
                if (cur == want || cur < (fps ? 10u : 1u) || cur > (fps ? 120u : 4u)) continue;
                snprintf(was, sizeof was, "%u", cur);
            }
            uint32_t *p = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)a;
            dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p); __atomic_store_n(p, want, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
            if (nlog[r] < 8) { nlog[r]++; char now[24];
                if (L->kind == MS_F32) snprintf(now, sizeof now, "%.3f ms (%d fps)", ms_want(row_target), row_target);
                else if (L->kind == SECS_F32) snprintf(now, sizeof now, "%.5f s (%d fps)", 1.0 / row_target, row_target);
                else if (L->kind == TICKS_U32) snprintf(now, sizeof now, "%u (%d fps)", want, row_target);
                else if (L->kind == MODE_U32) snprintf(now, sizeof now, "1 (%d fps)", row_target);
                else snprintf(now, sizeof now, "%u%s", L->kind == FPS_F32 ? (unsigned)row_target : want, L->kind == FPS_F32 || L->kind == FPS_I32 ? " fps" : " vsyncs");
                LOG("main: %s%s %s → %s (%s)", L->what, L->copies > 1 ? (c ? " (render thread)" : " (game thread)") : "", was, now, src); }
        }
    }
}

// The Mac's DM_CTL "cvarf <main offset> <value>" (hle_hid.c), for trying an Unreal console variable while the game runs: the TAutoConsoleVariable at main+offset holds at +0x10
// the pointer to its value, the game thread's copy then the render thread's; both are set to the float
void dm_ctl_cvar_f32(uint64_t off, float v) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmod; i++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].name, "main")) {
        uint64_t obj; if (!rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(g_mod[i].base + off + 0x10), &obj, sizeof obj) || !obj) { LOG("DM_CTL: cvarf main+%#llx: no value pointer yet", (unsigned long long)off); return; }
        for (int c = 0; c < 2; c++) { float *p = (float *)(uintptr_t)(obj + 4 * (uint64_t)c); dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p); *p = v; }
        LOG("DM_CTL: cvarf main+%#llx = %g (both copies at %#llx)", (unsigned long long)off, v, (unsigned long long)obj);
    }
}
// "peek <guest address> <count>": count floats (and their bits) from guest memory, read safely, to the log
void dm_ctl_peek(uint64_t a, int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n && i < 64; i += 4) {
        uint32_t w[4] = {0}; int k = n - i < 4 ? n - i : 4;
        if (!rd(a + 4 * (uint64_t)i, w, 4 * (size_t)k)) { LOG("DM_CTL: peek %#llx: not readable", (unsigned long long)(a + 4 * (uint64_t)i)); return; }
        float f[4]; memcpy(f, w, sizeof f);
        LOG("DM_CTL: peek %#llx: %g %g %g %g (%08x %08x %08x %08x)", (unsigned long long)(a + 4 * (uint64_t)i), f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3], w[0], w[1], w[2], w[3]);
    }
}
// "memdump <guest address> <bytes> <path>": guest memory to a file, read safely (stops at the first unreadable page)
void dm_ctl_memdump(uint64_t a, uint64_t n, const char *path) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "wb"); if (!f) { LOG("[RED] DM_CTL: memdump: cannot open %s", path); return; }
    static uint8_t buf[1 << 16]; uint64_t done = 0;
    while (done < n) { size_t k = n - done < sizeof buf ? (size_t)(n - done) : sizeof buf; if (!rd(a + done, buf, k)) break; fwrite(buf, 1, k, f); done += k; }
    fclose(f); LOG("DM_CTL: memdump %#llx: %llu of %llu bytes → %s", (unsigned long long)a, (unsigned long long)done, (unsigned long long)n, path);
}
// "cvari <main offset> <value>": the same for an int console variable
void dm_ctl_cvar_i32(uint64_t off, int32_t v) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nmod; i++) if (!strcmp(g_mod[i].name, "main")) {
        uint64_t obj; if (!rd((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)(g_mod[i].base + off + 0x10), &obj, sizeof obj) || !obj) { LOG("DM_CTL: cvari main+%#llx: no value pointer yet", (unsigned long long)off); return; }
        for (int c = 0; c < 2; c++) { int32_t *p = (int32_t *)(uintptr_t)(obj + 4 * (uint64_t)c); dm_guest_write_prepare(p, sizeof *p); *p = v; }
        LOG("DM_CTL: cvari main+%#llx = %d (both copies at %#llx)", (unsigned long long)off, v, (unsigned long long)obj);
    }
}
